title: Beabadobee Blasts to No. 1 on ARIA Chart With ‘Pylon’
summary: "Pylon" is the Filipino-British singer and songwriter’s fourth studio album and first leader.
contentText:
Beabadoobee bags her first chart crown in Australia as Pylon (via Dirty Hit/Inertia) debuts in the top spot.

Pylon is the Filipino-British singer and songwriter’s fourth studio album and second top 10 appearance on the ARIA Albums Chart , after 2024’s This Is How Tomorrow Moves , which peaked at No. 6. The indie-pop artist is booked to play arenas on her The Powerlines Tour of Australia in early 2027.

Coming in at No. 2 on the new chart, published Friday, Sept. 25, is Miley Cyrus ’ Bass Persuades (Atlantic/Warner). It’s Miley’s eighth appearance in the national top 10 (not including her work as Hannah Montana), a tally that includes No. 1s with 2008’s Breakout , 2013’s Bangerz and 2023’s Endless Summer Vacation .

C.O.F.F.I.N. nails a top 10 appearance with Out In Oslo (p(doom) records/Inertia) , the Sydney punk rock act’s sixth studio album. It’s new at No. 8, easily the band’s best chart effort. Until now, C.O.F.F.I.N.’s career peak position was Australia Stops , which hit No. 47 in 2023.

Also flying into the top 10 is Lizzy McAlpine ’s Angel (RCA/Sony), new at No. 10. That’s a new career high for the Pennsylvania-born artist, whose 2024 collection Older reached No. 26.

The latest all-genres top 50 features a slew of new arrivals. Among them, recordings by U.S. country singer Riley Green ( That’s Just Me at No. 14 via Big Machine/Universal), metal legends Anthrax ( Cursum Perficio at No. 24 via Nuclear Blast/Universal), Briggs’ heavy rock act Big Noter ( Songs In The Key Of Wrestling at No. 30 via Island/Universal), Carly Rae Jepsen ( Day and Night at No. 31 via Interscope/Universal), Tove Lo ( Estrus at No. 32 via Virgin Music Group/Inertia), Beck ( Ride Lonesome at No. 33 via Capitol/Universal), Daniel Pemberton ( Project Hail Mary — Original Motion Picture Score at No. 47 via Milan Records/Sony) and Orville Peck ( Mule at No. 49 via Warner).

Over on the ARIA Singles Chart , Ella Langley ’s “Choosin’ Texas” (Sony) racks up a 15th non-consecutive week at No. 1. In the United States earlier this week, “Choosin’ Texas” topped the Billboard Hot 100 for a 23rd week — breaking the record for the longest No. 1 run in the chart’s history.

Finally, Adéla has two reasons to celebrate. The Slovak artist has a pair of singles in ARIA top 10 for the first time: “Nicole Kidman” up 14-4 and “Ain’t In LA” up 13-7 (both via Capitol/Universal).
